name: Çatalhöyük roof-access settlement
description: Closely clustered houses at Çatalhöyük often had access from the roof. Excavation traces in Building 1 suggest a ladder near the oven, while a blocked doorway in Building 3 suggests that some buildings also had ground-level access in certain phases.

impact.note: One settlement's way of packing houses without streets, a local arrangement of housing with no known later building tradition descending from it.

date.label: Eastern mound occupation approximately 7400–6200 BCE
date.basis: The stated range or year applies to the described evidence or documentary event; it does not establish invention.

events.statement: The site description reports 18 occupation levels on the eastern mound dated 7400–6200 BCE and clustered roof-access houses.

evidence.supports: The site description reports 18 occupation levels on the eastern mound dated 7400–6200 BCE and clustered roof-access houses.
The excavation reports curved plaster to accommodate a feature such as a ladder and heavily trampled floor near the proposed roof access.
The project director reports the blocked entrance found in Building 3 and interprets it as ground-level access in at least some phases.
The site description reports 18 occupation levels on the eastern mound dated 7400–6200 BCE and clustered roof-access houses.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced event for this particular case, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: The interval dates the eastern mound occupation. Roof access is inferred from local archaeological traces, and a blocked doorway in Building 3 gives evidence for another access arrangement.

research.note: Independent source review checked the dated event and its stated scope; see the caveats for the limits of the dating. Additional excavation reports document the inferred ladder area and the counterexample of a blocked ground-level doorway.
